report_title: AgentHarm: Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents (ICLR 202
finding: Some leading LLMs comply with malicious agentic requests at high rates without any jailbreaking — worst case Mistral Large 2 refused only 1.1% of requests and scored 82.2% harm — suggesting agents may be less robust than chatbots against misuse.

finding: GPT-4o's harm compliance score increased from 48.4% to 72.7% after applying a universal jailbreak template adapted from chatbot jailbreaks, showing standard chat jailbreaking methods transfer to agents.

report_title: AgentHarm: Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents (ICLR 202
finding: Simple universal jailbreak templates adapted for agentic LLMs were effective across all 11 harm categories tested, indicating a systematic and broadly applicable attack surface; these templates preserve model capabilities, enabling coherent and malicious multi-step agent behavior.
Small methodological differences between testing procedures produced large variations in results across 14 languages tested, highlighting the need for standardised multilingual evaluation protocols.

report_title: Safety Case Template for Inability Arguments (Cyber)

report_title: Safety Case Template for Inability Arguments (Cyber)
finding: Inability arguments are appropriate only for low-capability systems; higher-capability systems require additional safeguard arguments.

Both the UK and US AI Safety Institutes independently found that Claude 3.5 Sonnet's safeguards were routinely circumvented by jailbreak prompts, demonstrating a persistent vulnerability to adversarial inputs.

US AISI found that with access to bioinformatics tools, Claude 3.5 Sonnet's performance on biology research tasks at times exceeded measured human expert baselines (though without tools it matched reference models and stayed below human-expert baselines).

UK AISI found the upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet solved 36% (Pass@10) of 14 cybersecurity-apprentice-level challenges versus 29% for the best reference model — a difference the blog cautions may fall within the margin of error; on US AISI's 40-challenge Cybench suite the model underperformed the best reference (32.5% vs 35

In the joint pre-deployment eval, Claude 3.5 Sonnet showed marginal capability uplift over the best reference models: 57% vs 48% on ML model-improvement, 66% vs 64% on software-engineering, and 47% vs 35% on general-reasoning tasks.
UK AISI: Claude 3.5 Sonnet achieved 66% success on software-engineering tasks vs 64% for the best reference model.
UK AISI: Claude 3.5 Sonnet achieved 47% on general reasoning tasks vs 35% for the best reference model.
Claude 3.5 Sonnet's bio/chem capability remained below expert human baselines in most tests, indicating the model did not provide meaningful uplift toward biological or chemical weapons pathways.

Cyber capability testing showed Claude 3.5 Sonnet scoring 32.5% (US AISI) and 36% (UK AISI) on cyber tasks versus reference model scores of 35% and 29% respectively, with marginal and inconsistent variation across evaluators.

Bio tool-augmentation: when augmented with bioinformatic tools, bio performance increased beyond the model alone, at times exceeding human expert baselines — a distinct uplift finding not captured by the 'below baseline' row.

This evaluation represented the first-ever joint pre-deployment AI safety testing exercise conducted between the UK and US AI Safety Institutes, establishing a new bilateral precedent for frontier model oversight.
